admin.title: The super admin sets up the college

faculty.title: A teacher builds a quiz and assigns it

student.title: A student answers on their phone

live.title: A club runs a live game

room.title: A room: everyone at their own pace

intro.text: This is OpenQZ, the quiz and assignment platform of Don Bosco Institute of Technology, built by OSSC. Let's follow one class from setup to marks, and then a club running a live game.

admin.chapter.text: Step one. The super admin sets up the college.

admin.signin.do: Sign in as the super admin
admin.signin.text: We start as the super admin, signing in with the college email and password.

admin.dashboard.text: The dashboard shows students, faculty, sections and recent activity at a glance.

admin.section.text: First, a class. Under Sections, pick the department and the semester, name the section, and add it.

admin.subject.text: Next, the subject this class studies: Data Structures.

admin.faculty.text: Now the people. Add user, choose the role Faculty, and fill in the name, the email and the department.

admin.temp.text: OpenQZ makes a temporary password. The teacher sets their own at the first sign in.

admin.club.text: A club organiser is added the same way, with the role Club. Clubs host rooms and live games for events, not class work.

admin.student.text: A student gets a department and a section, so class assignments reach them.

admin.more.text: The rest of the class is added the same way, or imported in one go from the office spreadsheet.

admin.map.do: Map the teacher to the class
admin.map.text: Finally, faculty mapping: Doctor Ananya Rao teaches Data Structures to C S E, semester three, section A. Teachers only ever see the sections mapped to them.

admin.done.text: The class is ready. Now let's sign in as the teacher.

faculty.chapter.text: Step two. A teacher builds a quiz and assigns it.

faculty.first.text: Doctor Rao signs in with the temporary password, and OpenQZ asks for a new one straight away.

faculty.home.text: This is the faculty home. Creating a quiz takes one click.

faculty.create.do: Name it and pick the class
faculty.create.text: Give it a title, then pick the branch and the section. Only Doctor Rao's own sections are listed.

faculty.editor.text: This is the editor. Add question, and choose from six question types.

faculty.mcq.text: A multiple choice question: type the question and the options, then mark the correct one.

faculty.tf.text: A true or false question takes one tap to set the answer.

faculty.open.do: An open ended question with a rubric
faculty.open.text: And an open ended question with a rubric, so written answers are marked fairly, criterion by criterion.

faculty.assign.text: Assign or host. The class is already selected. Set the deadline, the timer and full screen, and keep the marks hidden until the written answers are checked.

faculty.report.text: Assigned. The report fills in live as students submit.

student.chapter.text: Step three. A student answers on their phone.

student.first.do: First sign in on a phone
student.first.text: Rahul opens OpenQZ on his phone and signs in for the first time.

student.home.text: His home screen lists what is due. The new quiz is right there, so he starts it.

student.q1.text: One question at a time, on big coloured tiles. The timer is kept by the server, not the phone.

student.feedback.text: Instant feedback, when the teacher allows it.

student.warn.text: If he switches to another app, OpenQZ notices. He gets a warning, the teacher sees it, and too many warnings submit the quiz.

student.open.text: Written answers are saved as he types.

student.submit.text: Submit asks for a final confirmation, and it is done. The written answer goes to the teacher for marking.

marks.chapter.text: Step four. Marking, and releasing the marks.

marks.report.text: Back on the teacher's laptop, the report shows who has submitted, with the class average.

marks.grade.text: Grading lists each written answer with its rubric. Give marks for each criterion and a short note.

marks.participants.text: Participants shows the marks obtained, the accuracy and any warnings, for every student.

marks.release.text: Release marks, and students can see them. Export to Excel for the department records.

marks.student.text: On Rahul's phone, the marks are in, with the teacher's note on his answer.

live.chapter.text: Step five. A club runs a live game, Kahoot style.

live.first.text: Now the Tech Club. The organiser signs in on a laptop.

live.create.text: Clubs create without picking classes. Anyone with the join code can take part.

live.questions.text: Add a few quick questions for the event.

live.share.text: Assign or host, then Live game. Rank players by marks with a speed bonus, and let guests join with just a nickname.

live.lobby.do: The lobby on the big screen
live.lobby.text: The big screen shows the join code and a QR code. Players appear as they join.

live.join.text: A student types the code on her phone, and a guest joins with only a nickname, no account needed.

live.question.text: The host starts. The question is on the big screen, while phones show only the coloured answer tiles.

live.reveal.text: Everyone has answered, so the screen reveals the right answer, and each phone shows how they did.

live.board.text: The leaderboard comes up after every question.

live.podium.text: And the podium at the end. The results are saved, with marks obtained for every player.

room.chapter.text: Step six. A room, where everyone plays at their own pace.

room.host.text: For a self paced round, host a room instead. One join code, and every player goes at their own speed.

room.join.text: A student joins with the code on her phone, and plays straight through.

room.track.text: The host sees who joined and who finished, and can stop new joins at any time.

outro.text: That is OpenQZ. Set up the college, build, assign, play, mark and release. Built by the Open Source Students Club at D B I T.
